backgrounds: Two connected outdoor settings representing a single continuous location/night-time convenience-store scene: (1) the storefront entrance, with glass double doors, a bright fluorescent-lit interior of shelves/aisles visible through the glass, and a low brick ledge/step where the two characters sit; and (2) a slightly wider shot of the same sidewalk area outside the store, softly lit by a warm street lamp against a dark, blurred night background (bushes, a lamp post, a dark building facade). Both are the same set filmed from different angles/framings rather than distinct locations — a single stationary two-shot conversation scene bookended by black title/credit cards ('Low Battery People' logo cards) with no set at all.
props: smartphone held by the female character
soft-serve ice cream cone held by the male character
two white paper shopping bags with handles resting on the ledge beside the characters
round black-framed glasses on the male character
brick ledge/step the characters sit on
glass storefront double doors with store signage
lighting_notes: Storefront scenes use bright, even fluorescent interior light spilling through the glass doors as a backlight/rim source, silhouette-adjacent but with faces still lit softly from the front; the exterior sidewalk cutaways drop to a darker, moodier night-time look with a single warm practical light (street lamp) creating a soft glow against near-black negative space. The contrast between bright storefront and dark night sidewalk is used to distinguish the two camera setups within the same scene.
color_palette: charcoal/black (male character's coat and night background)
bright yellow (title card text and 'NEW EPISODE DAILY' tape graphic)
white (paper shopping bags, ice cream, title card subtext)
visual_complexity_notes: The set is minimal and deliberately narrow in scope: essentially one static two-character sitting/standing setup shot from two angles, plus plain black title/credit cards with stylized yellow serif text. Background store shelving is present but kept soft-focus/blurred so it reads as texture rather than detail, keeping visual focus entirely on the two stop-motion character faces and their exaggerated expressions/reactions, consistent with a low-budget, character-reaction-driven comedic format.
